source: Kim, Huang, Reza, Grand (2025) Chopping Trees: Semantic Similarity Based Dynamic Pruning for Tree-of-Thought Reasoning (SSDP)
finding: Pruning by merging near-duplicate thought nodes (not by low score) cuts cost with small accuracy loss. This avoids the false-negative risk of score-based cuts.
numbers: Up to 2.3x speedup over strong tree-search baselines on GSM8K and MATH500; 85-90% fewer nodes explored; accuracy typically within 5% of the best baseline.
limits: Abstract page only. No false-negative rate and no equal-compute baseline reported there. NeurIPS 2025 workshop paper.
agent_relevance: Gap 4/6. Prune duplicates, not bad-looking branches: a safer default prune rule.

source: Wang et al. (2025) Thoughts Are All Over the Place (TIP: thought-switching penalty), Table 3
finding: A decoding penalty on switch tokens ('alternatively') raised accuracy and cut switches, so holding a thought longer helps reasoning models.
numbers: alpha=3, beta=600 tokens (grid alpha {3,5,10,20,30}, beta {300..700}; chosen on AIME 2022-23 dev, QwQ 39.8%). AIME2024 QwQ-32B 38.3 -> 44.1 pass@1; R1-Distill-32B 61.4 -> 64.1; DeepSeek-R1 73.8 -> 74.8 (prompt-only version 72.4). MATH500-Hard 83.1 -> 83.7; GPQA 57.6 -> 59.1. Switch tokens e.g. QwQ AIME 16.1 -> 13.9, DeepSeek-R1 13.8 -> 5.7.
limits: Decoding change, not a prompt. Paper reports no separate minimum-hold finding; the prompt-only version did not help DeepSeek-R1.
agent_relevance: Gap 7. A hold of about 600 tokens before a switch is allowed beat no hold; a prompt asking for it did not.

source: Wang et al. (2025) TIP, Table 2 sweep of penalty duration beta
finding: Longer hold is not always better. At strong penalty (alpha=20), extending beta beyond 300 lowered accuracy.
numbers: alpha=20: beta above 300 gave lower dev accuracy; best setting alpha=3, beta=600 (weak penalty, long window).
limits: Dev set sweep on one model (QwQ-32B-Preview). Exact table cells not extracted.
agent_relevance: Gap 7. Over-holding also hurts: a mild, bounded hold is the sweet spot; a hard lock is not.

source: Qian et al. (2026) PAC-CF, TSP50 evaluator misranking stress test
finding: Repeating the evaluator 16 times does not fix systematic misranking. On conflict frontiers (where the evaluator is misled) the correct step is removed more, not less.
numbers: TSP50, 24 instances, K=4: control frontiers reference action removed 54.2% (R=1) vs 52.1% (R=16); conflict frontiers 57.5% vs 64.4%. Reference path survives top-4 pruning in 0/24 conflict vs 4/24 control tasks; top-6: 1/24 vs 8/24. Other task: GTA tool planning N=99.
limits: Evaluator noise level not swept; no best-of-N baseline; Appendix E not read. Three task families only.
agent_relevance: Gap 4. The rate of cutting the right branch is high (50-65% per step at K=4) when the scorer is biased; resampling the scorer does not cure it. Needs an outside check.

source: Snell et al. (2024) Scaling LLM test-time compute optimally can be more effective than scaling model parameters
finding: With a process reward model, beam search beats best-of-N at small budgets, then loses its edge and often falls below best-of-N at large budgets. Easy questions get worse with search.
numbers: MATH, budgets 4/16/64/256. Levels 1-2: beam degrades with budget (PRM exploitation). Levels 3-4: beam beats best-of-N. Level 5: little progress either way. Lookahead search costs N(k+1) samples and underperforms. Over-optimised search yields 1-2 step solutions.
limits: Exact accuracies only in figures. PaLM-2 class models and a learned PRM, not 2025-26 reasoning models.
agent_relevance: Gap 6. Pruning by a learned score pays on mid-hard items at low budget, can hurt on easy items at high budget. Gate pruning on difficulty and budget.

source: Wu et al. (2024) Inference scaling laws (REBASE tree search vs sampling)
finding: A reward-balanced tree search reaches higher accuracy than plain sampling with weighted voting at fewer FLOPs. MCTS did not.
numbers: MATH500 weighted voting: Mistral-7B Rebase 32 samples 45.0% at 1.36e14 FLOPs vs sampling 256 samples 42.8% at 8.70e14. Llemma-34B Rebase 32: 49.2% (7.08e14) vs sampling 64: 46.7% (12.1e14). Matched samples: Rebase +1.9 to +5.3 points MATH500, +0.7 to 1.9 GSM8K. MCTS underperforms the sampling methods at each compute budget.
limits: Small open models, 2024; FLOPs from the generator only. Gains shrink on easy items.
agent_relevance: Gap 6. An equal-compute win for pruning exists but depends on the pruner design (balanced, not greedy).

source: CodeTree authors (2024) CodeTree: agent-guided tree search for code generation
finding: Code tree where execution results plus an LLM critic decide refine, abort or accept. Abort sends the search back to sibling nodes (a weak form of revival). Removing abort evaluation or solution check costs most.
numbers: GPT-4o-mini HumanEval/HumanEval+: full 94.5/84.8; no solution verification 91.5/81.7; no node-abort evaluation 91.5/81.1; execution output only (no node scoring) 92.7/82.1. HumanEval vs Reflexion 92.1, Resample 89.0. SWE-bench: CodeTree 27.6 vs Reflexion 25.3 vs CoT 23.6.
limits: Budget fixed at 20 samples per task, no token accounting. Does not isolate execution-only pruning from the critic self-score beyond one ablation. Visible tests only.
agent_relevance: Gap 3. Mixing a real test result with a critic beat test-output-only by 1.8 points; this is not a clean answer to outside signal vs self-score at equal tokens.

source: Muennighoff et al. (2025) s1: simple test-time scaling
finding: Sequential extra thinking (Wait) beats parallel majority voting for their model; tree search REBASE scales past the context limit.
numbers: s1-32B AIME24 56.7%; about 57% at about 7,320 thinking tokens; Wait lifts 50% to 57%; flat after about 6x base budget. REBASE vs majority voting: 16 trajectories, 30 AIME24 questions, REBASE better. Sequential at 512 steps overflowed context on 12 of 30 questions.
limits: Exact equal-token numbers only in figures. REBASE token counts exclude reward model compute.
agent_relevance: Gap 6. On a 2025 reasoning model, continuing one line longer beats parallel voting; pruning-based search wins only when context is the limit.

source: Chen, Li, Cakir, Akcali, Lee, Mattar (2026) Extracting Search Trees from LLM Reasoning Traces
finding: In four-in-a-row, 14 reasoning models search shallow. Breadth, not depth, predicts winning. More reasoning effort gave larger trees and more wins.
numbers: Mean max depth 1.78 plies (SD 0.71; per model 1.00-3.48) vs human estimate 4-6. Breadth beta=0.075, p=0.0025; depth beta=-0.015, p=0.82. GPT-OSS-120B high vs medium effort: bigger trees, higher win rate (numbers only in figure). Causal cut on Qwen3-Next-80B-Thinking: chosen branch removed changes move 32.0%; largest unchosen branch 1.2%.
limits: One game, no backtracking analysis, no loss-triggered pruning. Depth by difficulty not studied.
agent_relevance: Gap 2. LLM trees grow with effort but in breadth; the human loss/no-loss gap rising with depth (34/40/49%) has no LLM counterpart yet.

source: Coda-Forno et al. (2024) Inducing anxiety in large language models can induce bias (abstract re-opened)
finding: Anxiety text raised questionnaire anxiety and bias; more anxious text gave more bias. Tested on a bias benchmark, not a planning or loss task.
numbers: 12 LLMs given STICSA; 6 answered consistently with human-like scores. Details beyond the abstract (beta=0.08, p=.02) are from evidence c19.
limits: Abstract only this session. No pruning or planning outcome.
agent_relevance: Gap 8. Anxiety framing moves some models on bias tasks; whether it changes branch cutting is untested.

source: Sezener, Dezfouli, Keramati (2019) as resource-rational stand-in while Callaway is unread
finding: Only the earlier rational-use rule is available: stop deepening when expected value of more search falls under its time cost.
numbers: See evidence b20 (2000 ms vs 700 ms groups; shallower plan under pressure). No numeric threshold comparable to the fitted gamma_S of about 0.6.
limits: Not re-opened this session; no comparison to gamma_S exists in what we read.
